STEP 1 - Scene: This appears to be a single half of a small yellow fruit or vegetable (looks like a cut passion fruit or small squash-like piece with a pale, seedy/fibrous interior) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above (overhead view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 × (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm² for a round equivalent; a square plate of 20 cm side is about 400 cm², but the rim is rounded, so I use ~350 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One item: a halved yellow fruit (about 5 cm diameter, roughly 2.5 cm tall) with visible white pulp and seeds, consistent with a cut passion fruit half or similar small yellow fruit. Treating it as a yellow fruit with pale flesh.

STEP 4 - Area: The fruit covers about 5 cm × 5 cm ≈ 20 cm², roughly 6% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: 20 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 50 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Fruit pieces bulk density ~0.6 g/ml → about 30 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Assuming passion-fruit-like pulp/flesh at ~97 kcal/100 g (the sweet pulp with seeds is energy-dense relative to its mass; a more typical whole-fruit value would be lower, ~60 kcal/100 g). Using ~70 kcal/100 g as a middle estimate: 30 g × 0.70 ≈ 21 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single half of a small fruit weighing ~30 g and ~20 kcal is plausible for what is visible. No other food is on the plate.
